summary: All three Basic Sole Trader runs read as credible accounts for the trades described: the bricklayer shows materials/stock, sub-contract direct costs and van costs; the IT consultancy shows wages, premises and a high gross margin explained by the sheet layout; the taxi driver's largest cost is motor expenses. The only oddities are presentational quirks the scenario notes or minor scale points, none of which block the runs.

concerns.figure: Employee Costs £0 and Premises Costs £0 (P&L, cells C11/C12) in bst-brickwork-pro-nonvat
concerns.where: Profit & Loss Account, BrickWork Pro run
concerns.why: A building trader with no wages and no premises cost looks thin at first sight, but the scenario states there is no payroll and no employee-costs or premises code in the purchase journal (labour is bought in as direct costs, code d £20,000). It reconciles to the journal, so this is a note only.

concerns.figure: Fixed Assets "New Asset Cost (Plant & Machinery)" £1,800 against Total Original Cost £39,000 (cells E67 / E1) in bst-scenario-basic
concerns.where: Fixed Assets section, Precision Code run
concerns.why: The single displayed addition row is only £1,800 while the schedule total is £39,000 across three additions. The report's own check labels E67 as "first addition recorded" so the presentation is by design, but a reader glancing at the schedule sees a figure twenty times smaller than the total. Worth a look, not a blocker.

concerns.figure: Income Tax line £0 on the P&L (cell C30) in all three runs, with tax shown on the "Tax at basic rate" line beneath it
concerns.where: Profit & Loss Account, all three runs
concerns.why: The P&L Income Tax row reads zero while the actual charge (£1,792 / £78,035 / £3,808.40) appears on the basic-rate row below and flows correctly into Net Income After Tax and the SA103S. Self-consistent and the tax chain reconciles, so presentational only.

concerns.figure: Advertising £4,560 equal to Legal & Professional £4,560 (cells C17/C18) in bst-scenario-basic
concerns.where: Profit & Loss Account, Precision Code run
concerns.why: Two unrelated expense lines carrying an identical figure suggests the same journal code (l 4,560.00) may have been mapped to both rows; total expenses still tie to the journal, so this is a coding question rather than a mis-statement.

concerns.figure: Stock opening £10,000 / closing £6,000 and Cost of Sales £10,540 in an IT consultancy (bst-scenario-basic)
concerns.where: Stock section and P&L cell C6, Precision Code run
concerns.why: Stock in a software/consultancy business is unusual, but at £6k-£10k against £409,900 turnover it is immaterial and is not the largest cost (employee costs £69,200 are), so the trade still matches the accounts.
